papers_read.title_as_printed: Development and validation of a nomogram for predicting mild cognitive impairment in middle-aged and elderly people (Huang et al., Asian J Psychiatry 2022)
Association of Qi-stagnation constitution and subjective sleep characteristics with mild cognitive impairment among elderly in community: A cross-sectional study (Liu et al., Eur J Integr Med 2023)

what_each_reports.P-258: Cross-sectional Rugao (Jiangsu) sample of 478 adults aged 48-85 (387 MoCA-defined MCI, 91 without; MCI = MoCA < 25). A LASSO + stepwise logistic nomogram with age, gender, residence, education and reading has apparent AUC 0.8704 and mean 10-fold CV AUC 0.8353. Sleep quality and insomnia were among 42 candidate predictors but were not among the univariately significant factors.
what_each_reports.P-261: Cross-sectional Fuzhou (Fujian) sample of 1,071 adults aged 55-75 without depression (314 MCI, 29.3%; MoCA-based). After adjustment for age, sex and education, the joint exposure sleep disturbance (PSQI >= 6) plus Qi-stagnation constitution has OR 2.581 (95% CI 1.706-3.907) for MCI vs neither; no additive interaction (RERI 0.167, CI -1.154 to 1.488). Its own logistic models of Qi-stagnation, sleep latency and daytime dysfunction have AUC 0.602-0.683.

quantity_a: Discrimination (ROC-AUC) of a five-predictor demographic/lifestyle nomogram for concurrent MoCA-defined MCI in Rugao adults 48-85.
quantity_b: Adjusted odds ratio of MCI for the joint exposure 'sleep disturbance and Qi-stagnation' vs neither, in non-depressed Fuzhou adults 55-75.
incompatible_if_same: Not applicable: an AUC of a prediction model and an odds ratio for one exposure are different metric types on different predictor sets. The only overlapping construct (sleep and MCI) is significant in P-261 and non-significant in P-258's univariate screen, which is a significance-only difference under Section 5.2 and not a data conflict; the exposure definitions also differ (P-258 dichotomous self-reported sleep quality/insomnia; P-261 PSQI total >= 6 and PSQI components).

gates.task: nominal match only (record says T6 for both; the registry codes P-258 as T1 risk prediction and P-261 as T6 association)
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: separate Chinese community samples (MPLC Rugao vs Fuzhou day-care centres); the record itself sets dataset_equal = No
gates.validation_tier: n/a for P-261 (association study, no model validated); P-258 is internally cross-validated (V2)
gates.modality_family: match: questionnaire/clinical tabular data in both

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: ROC-AUC vs odds ratio; different predictor sets; MCI operationalised differently (MoCA < 25 with education correction in P-258; MoCA with education-dependent cut-offs plus clinical criteria in P-261)
performance_validity: not a performance comparison (one side is an odds ratio); P-258 AUC 0.8704 is below the 0.97 threshold in any case
independence: Distinct studies, different cohorts and authors.
grounds: P-258's figure is the ROC-AUC of a nomogram built from age, gender, residence, education and reading.
P-261's figure is an adjusted odds ratio for a joint sleep-disturbance and Qi-stagnation exposure.
The two are different metric types on different predictors in different cohorts, and the record already fails its own dataset gate.
The one shared construct (sleep and MCI) differs only in statistical significance, which Section 5.2 says is not a data conflict.

evidence_quotes.quote: The model showed good discrimination power (area under receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) curve was 0.8704) and good calibration.
A total of 478 participants, including 270 males and 208 females in our study, were composed of 387 with MCI and 91 without MCI.
If the score was less than 25 points, it was defined as MCI.
the risk of suffering from MCI for older adults with sleep disturbance and Qi-stagnation was 2.581 times higher than that for those without sleep disturbance or Qi-stagnation

record_defects: The index/PDF map titles P-261 'Unveiling the sound of the cognitive status: machine learning-based speech analysis...', but the PDF text and registry row are the Liu et al. Qi-stagnation/sleep study; the map title is wrong, the PDF is the intended paper.
gap_magnitude 0.845 is computed between an AUC (0.8704) and an odds ratio (2.581), which is meaningless.
Task recorded as T6 for both, but the registry codes P-258 as T1 and its own claim is a prediction-model AUC.
resolution_status 'partially_resolved_candidate' rests on 'bridging evidence' (prevalences, an HR) that explains no disagreement; there is no disagreement to bridge.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Two studies reporting the same exposure-outcome odds ratio (e.g. PSQI-defined sleep disturbance and MoCA-defined MCI) with non-overlapping confidence intervals in comparable populations.
